planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun; Bedbug forms a vigorous diploid clump with reliable rebloom and heavy increase.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to light afternoon shade in hot climates. Bred by hybridizer Williams-S. and registered in 2019, Bedbug is a diploid miniature daylily bearing rust-toned blooms streaked with gold and edged with a slightly darker band, opening from dramatic dark buds marked with spots, stipples, and stripes. Flowers measure under 3 inches, held on 31-inch scapes in midseason with reliable rebloom and strong increase. The cultivar won the American Hemerocallis Society's Donn Fischer Memorial Cup, the top honor for miniature-flowered daylilies, in 2024. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain vigorous flowering.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun; Chickens on the Porch forms a dormant clump with heavy branching and bud count.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to light partial shade. Bred by Tim Herrington and registered in 2014, Chickens on the Porch is a fragrant, dormant miniature daylily with red blooms under 3 inches marked by darker red veining above a small green throat, carried on 22-inch scapes with heavy 7-way branching and 36-40 buds per scape. It reblooms reliably through the season and won the American Hemerocallis Society's Donn Fischer Memorial Cup for outstanding miniature-flowered daylily in 2023. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain heavy flowering.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun; Wayne and Coral's Love forms an evergreen clump that benefits from winter mulch in colder zones.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun. Bred by Netherton and registered in 2013 from a cross of Everybody Loves Earnest and Coffee to Go, Wayne and Coral's Love is a fragrant, evergreen diploid miniature daylily bearing orange-red blooms under 3 inches with darker veining, a dark red triangular eye, and a green throat, held on 22-inch scapes in early-midseason with reliable rebloom. It won the American Hemerocallis Society's Donn Fischer Memorial Cup for outstanding miniature-flowered daylily in 2022. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain heavy flowering.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun; Grandpa's Little Sweetheart forms a dormant clump with heavy branching and bud count.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to light partial shade. Bred by Katisue Herrington from a cross of Two Thumbs Up and (Everybody Loves Earnest x Janice Brown), and registered around 2010, Grandpa's Little Sweetheart is a dormant diploid miniature daylily with dark rose blooms under 3 inches featuring a red eyezone above a yellow-green throat, carried on 20-inch scapes with 32 buds and 7 branches in midseason with reliable rebloom. It won the American Hemerocallis Society's Donn Fischer Memorial Cup for outstanding miniature-flowered daylily in 2020. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain heavy flowering.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun; Raspberry Ripple Cupcake forms a dormant clump of fully double blooms.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to light partial shade. Bred by Tim Herrington, Raspberry Ripple Cupcake is a dormant diploid miniature daylily with fully double, cream-based blooms feathered in raspberry around the eye above a green throat, carried on 21-inch scapes in early-midseason with reliable rebloom. It won the American Hemerocallis Society's Donn Fischer Memorial Cup for outstanding miniature-flowered daylily in 2019. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain heavy flowering.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun; Lil' Black Buds forms a semi-evergreen clump that blooms especially early in the season.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun. Bred by Kenneth W. Begnaud and registered in 2009, Lil' Black Buds is a fragrant, semi-evergreen diploid miniature daylily with striking black-purple self-colored blooms above a green throat, carried on 22-inch scapes with 23 buds and 4 branches, blooming diurnally very early in the season with reliable rebloom. It won the American Hemerocallis Society's Donn Fischer Memorial Cup for outstanding miniature-flowered daylily in 2018, the Early Season Bloom Award in 2018, and the Lenington All-American Award in 2019. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain heavy flowering.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun; Spacecoast Tiny Perfection forms a compact clump prized for its perfectly round bloom form.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to light partial shade. Bred by John L. Kinnebrew Jr. as part of his Spacecoast series and registered in 1998, Spacecoast Tiny Perfection is a tetraploid miniature daylily with light peach-pink blooms under 3 inches, finished with wire-thin gold edges and green throats, prized for their perfectly round, wax-like substance. Flowers are held on 18-inch scapes in early-midseason. It won the American Hemerocallis Society's Donn Fischer Memorial Cup for outstanding miniature-flowered daylily in 2003. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain heavy flowering.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun; Everybody Loves Earnest forms a vigorous clump widely used as a parent in later award-winning miniatures.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to light partial shade. Bred by Tim Herrington and registered in 2005, Everybody Loves Earnest is a fragrant diploid miniature daylily with creamy apricot-pink blooms under 3 inches marked by a cherry-red eye above a lime-green throat, carried on 28-inch scapes with 7 branches, blooming early season with reliable rebloom. Named for Earnest Yearwood of Milledgeville, Georgia, a well-known figure in the daylily world, it won the American Hemerocallis Society's Donn Fischer Memorial Cup for outstanding miniature-flowered daylily in 2012 and an Award of Merit in 2013. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain heavy flowering.
